question: Which site is known for its elaborate dockyard structure?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lothal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lothal is a prominent site of the Indus Valley Civilization, located in present-day Gujarat, India.
 
• It is renowned for its advanced and elaborate dockyard structure, which showcases remarkable engineering and urban planning skills.
 
• The dockyard was used for maritime activities, including trade and transportation, making Lothal a significant trading hub during ancient times.
 
• The dockyard was constructed using bricks and stone, and it featured a sophisticated drainage system to manage water flow and prevent flooding.
 
• Excavations at Lothal also revealed evidence of bead-making, shell-working, and metallurgy, highlighting its industrial and commercial significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Valley Civilization (IVC):**

 
 
• The IVC flourished between 2500 BCE and 1900 BCE in the regions of present-day Pakistan and northwest India.
 
• It is known for its advanced urban planning, including well-laid streets, drainage systems, and standardized brick sizes.
 
• Major sites include Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Dholavira, and Lothal.
 
 
 
• **Lothal's Dockyard:**
 
 
• The dockyard measures approximately 218 meters in length and 37 meters in width.
 
• It is believed to have been connected to the Sabarmati River for facilitating trade and transport.
 
• The structure showcases the technical prowess of the civilization in water management and maritime engineering.
 
 
 
• **Trade and Economy:**
 
 
• Lothal was a center for trade in beads, semi-precious stones, and ornaments.
 
• Artifacts discovered at the site include tools, seals, and pottery, indicating robust commercial activities.
 
• Trade links extended to Mesopotamia and other regions, reflecting the global reach of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
 
 
• **Other Indus Valley Sites:**
 
 
• **Harappa:** Known for its granaries and urban planning.
 
• **Mohenjo-Daro:** Famous for its Great Bath and advanced drainage systems.
 
• **Dholavira:** Known for its water conservation techniques and unique layout.
